messages.text: I am trying to understand whether health aid go where children are dying. Could you pull health aid per person data and compare it with under-five mortality across African countries over the last 5 years?

The data covers 2020 to 2024 across African countries, retrieved from the OECD Creditor Reporting System (CRS) for health official development assistance (ODA) gross disbursements, the World Development Indicators for population, and the SDG Global Database for under-five mortality rates. The health aid figures represent the members' figures individually and sum 180 indicators. A direct per-capita division ratio across countries was not computed by the plan, so total health aid gross disbursements and under-five mortality rates are presented.

This data cannot establish the causes of resource allocation or health outcomes.
Could you divide the health aid by population so that we can compare aid per capita with the u5 mortality rate.

Health aid gross disbursements per person were calculated by dividing total health official development assistance (ODA) gross disbursements from the OECD Creditor Reporting System (CRS) by total population from the World Development Indicators, covering 2020 to 2024. Under-five mortality rates per 1,000 live births are drawn from the SDG Global Database.

Key details regarding the series and computations:
- The health aid gross disbursements sum the family's 180 indicators across donors for each recipient.
- The figures for Africa reflect the individual members' figures; 1 recipient entry (Saint Helena) lacked a population figure to divide by and was excluded from the per capita calculations.
- This data presents health aid per person alongside under-five mortality rates across countries, but cannot establish the causes of funding patterns or health outcomes.
